page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.12xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It supplies 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory totals 192.0 GB, which aligns with the typical general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core.

The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, enabling efficient data transfer across networked environments. Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring the use of external network-attached block storage for all non-volatile disk requirements. There are no graphics processing units (GPUs) included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the m8ib.12xlarge provides resource balance without the cost overhead associated with integrated local solid-state drives or accelerator hardware. The high baseline networking capacity offsets the lack of local disks by facilitating fast communication with remote volumes and distributed services. The configuration is best aligned with multi-tier enterprise web serving, backend application logic, container hosting, continuous integration runners, and ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores running at 3.9 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory to maintain a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Network throughput is rated at a baseline of 50 Gbps, ensuring fast data transfer across cloud services. The instance features no integrated local storage or discrete GPU hardware, directing persistent disk operations to remote network storage volumes. By avoiding the overhead of bundled physical drives or specialized hardware accelerators, the m8ib.12xlarge offers a balanced resource footprint. This architectural profile is suited for medium-to-large enterprise workloads, including web application clusters, microservice backends, batch processing, and continuous integration environments requiring steady CPU throughput and consistent network capacity.
